newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK activists protest to Japan over disputed islands.
newsitem.headline: HK activists protest to Japan over disputed islands.

text.p: A dozen Hong Kong activists on Tuesday staged a demonstration outside the Japanese consulate to protest against a recent landing by two Japanese on a disputed island group in the East China Sea.

Banner-waving demonstrators called for Tokyo to withdraw from the uninhabited islands, known in Japanese as the Senkakus and in Chinese as the Diaoyus, and left a petition outside Japan's mission in the central business district.
The protest was sparked by reports that two Japanese had visited the potentially resource-rich islands, which are also claimed by Taiwan.

It came just a day after four activists, including two Hong Kong legislators, were acquitted of assaulting three police officers outside the consulate during a protest over the islands' sovereignty last October.
The four are still awaiting a verdict on charges of unlawful assembly.
Officials in Tokyo said on Monday that a city assemblyman from Okinawa and a reporter had made a symbolic visit to the islands, which have long been a source of dispute between Beijing and Tokyo.
China on Tuesday urged Tokyo to prevent such visits and avoid damaging sensitive Sino-Japanese ties.

"We demand that the Japanese government adopt measures to prevent further violations of Chinese sovereignty and damage to Sino-Japanese relations," Foreign Ministry spokesman Cui Tiankai told a news briefing.

The dispute over the Diaoyus is one of the few issues that unites popular opinion in mainland China, its arch-rival Taiwan and the British colony of Hong Kong, which reverts to Chinese rule on July 1.
Tokyo's claim dates to 1895, when Japan defeated China and seized Taiwan and other territories. China has claimed sovereignty over the islands for centuries.
